intro: je … desto (or je … umso) links two comparatives: the more one thing grows, the more the other does. Each half has its own word order. The je-half is a subordinate clause: je + comparative + subject + … + verb at the end (Je länger ich hier wohne). The desto-half is a main clause whose first position is desto + comparative, so the verb follows immediately and the subject comes after it (desto besser gefällt mir die Stadt). umso means exactly the same as desto and is slightly more formal. The comparative can be an adverb (besser, lieber, öfter) or can carry a noun with it (desto mehr Steuern, desto weniger Probleme). Short versions without verbs are common in headlines and sayings: Je höher der Preis, desto höher die Erwartungen. The halves can also be swapped: Die Aufgabe wird umso schwieriger, je länger man wartet — then the main clause comes first and je introduces the subordinate clause at the end.
tips[0].title: je-half: verb last
tips[0].text: je + comparative + subject + rest + finite verb: Je länger ich wohne … Je besser du vorbereitet bist … Je öfter ich den Text lese … It is a subordinate clause, so the finite verb is the last word.
tips[0].check.why: The je-half is a subordinate clause, so the conjugated verb goes last.
tips[1].title: desto-half: comparative, then the verb
tips[1].text: desto + comparative (+ noun) fills position 1; the finite verb follows, then the subject: desto schneller sind wir da · desto mehr Steuern zahle ich · desto weniger Probleme gibt es.
tips[1].trap: English keeps subject before verb ("the sooner we are there"). German inverts: desto schneller sind wir da — never "desto schneller wir sind da".
tips[1].check.why: desto + comparative fills position 1, then the verb, then the subject.
tips[2].title: umso = desto; swapped order
tips[2].text: umso replaces desto without any change: je …, umso … . With the main clause first, umso usually stays inside it and je follows: Die Aufgabe wird umso schwieriger, je länger man wartet.
tips[2].check.why: With the main clause first, umso (or desto) stays in the main clause and je opens the second part.
tips[3].title: Two comparatives, two word orders
tips[3].text: First half ends with the verb; second half starts with desto + comparative + verb. Say it as a seesaw: Je mehr …, desto mehr.
tips[3].check.why: Both halves need a comparative, and the second half takes desto or umso, never je.

hook: Link two changes in one sentence (the longer you wait, the harder it gets) and get both word orders right.
